title: What is recognition of prior learning?
description: Recognition of prior learning (RPL) assesses existing skills and experience for credit toward a qualification. How it works, evidence rules, an example.
shortAnswer: A recognition of prior learning (RPL) assessment is the process of assessing the skills and knowledge a person has already gained, through formal study, work or life experience, against the requirements of a qualification or unit, and granting credit for what they can prove. European countries call it validation of non-formal and informal learning. Qualification frameworks treat RPL as an assessment that must meet the same standard as any other.
keyTakeaways: Definitions converge: Cedefop describes validation as identifying, documenting, assessing and certifying learning, and qualification frameworks such as the AQF define RPL as an assessment of formal, informal and non-formal learning to determine credit.
RPL is an assessment, not an exemption: evidence must be valid, sufficient, authentic and current.
Vocational rules can make it mandatory: US Registered Apprenticeship standards require advanced standing or credit for demonstrated competency, granted to all applicants equally.
Credit transfer is different: it recognizes completed equivalent units or qualifications without reassessing the person.

sections.heading: How is recognition of prior learning defined?

blocks.text: Many national and regional qualification systems recognize prior learning, under different names. In the European Union it is called validation of non-formal and informal learning. The European Centre for the Development of Vocational Training ([Cedefop](https://www.cedefop.europa.eu/en/projects/validation-non-formal-and-informal-learning)) describes systems that allow individuals to "identify, document, assess and certify" all forms of learning, and notes that the 2012 Council Recommendation on validation encourages Member States to put national validation arrangements in place.

The Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF) is a well documented example of the assessment view. Its [glossary](https://www.aqf.edu.au/publication/aqf-glossary) defines RPL as "an assessment process that involves assessment of an individual's relevant prior learning (including formal, informal and non-formal learning) to determine the credit outcomes of an individual application for credit." Credit, in the same glossary, reduces the amount of learning required to achieve a qualification.

The AQF Council's [explanation of RPL](https://www.aqf.edu.au/download/425/recognition-prior-learning/19/recognition-prior-learning/pdf) says RPL assessment should be the same standard as other assessment for the qualification, should recognize learning regardless of how, when and where it was acquired, and must ensure evidence is valid, authentic, current and sufficient.

sections.heading: How does the RPL process work?

blocks.text: The RPL process works by matching a person's evidence to the requirements of a unit or qualification, testing that evidence, and filling any gaps with training. The AQF Council's explanation lists typical stages, which broadly follow the identify, document, assess and certify sequence Cedefop describes:

items: Advise the applicant about the process.
Give the applicant enough information to prepare evidence to the required standard.
Assess using appropriate evidence gathering methods and tools.
Report to internal and external stakeholders.

blocks.text: Methods named in the AQF explanation include mapping prior learning outcomes to the qualification components, oral or written questioning, observation in work based or simulated settings, challenge assessments and third party reports or work products.

sections.heading: What do vocational training standards require for RPL?

blocks.text: Regulated vocational systems turn RPL from good practice into a rule. In the United States, federal standards for Registered Apprenticeship require program standards to provide for "the granting of advanced standing or credit for demonstrated competency, acquired experience, training, or skills for all applicants equally", with commensurate wages for any progression step granted ([29 CFR 29.5(b)(12)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/subtitle-A/part-29/section-29.5)).

sections.heading: How is RPL different from credit transfer and verification of competency?

blocks.text: RPL is one of the defining features of [competency-based training](/glossary/competency-based-training): because the standard, not the time spent, is what matters, evidence gained anywhere can count.

sections.heading: What does an RPL application look like?

blocks.text: Illustrative example: an experienced aged care worker without a formal qualification applies for RPL.

items: **Mapping:** the assessor maps the worker's duties statement and training records against each unit's performance and knowledge evidence.
**Evidence:** supervisor reports, a portfolio of de-identified care plans and a workplace observation.
**Testing:** a competency conversation probes knowledge gaps; the assessor checks that evidence is recent and the worker's own.
**Outcome:** RPL granted for most units; gap training and assessment for two units where evidence was insufficient.
**Record:** the mapping, evidence, questions and decision are retained with the same rigour as any assessment.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Because Knowledge Foundry holds each program as a framework of competencies and assessment points, prior evidence can be mapped to specific points rather than to whole courses. Only the unmet points need training, and each credit decision keeps a traceable record.

faqs.q: Is RPL easier than doing the course?
faqs.a: It should not be. RPL removes unnecessary training, not assessment. The AQF Council's explanation says RPL assessment should be the same standard as other assessment for the qualification, with evidence that is valid, authentic, current and sufficient.

faqs.q: What counts as evidence for RPL?
faqs.a: Anything that validly shows current skills and knowledge against the unit requirements: work samples, position descriptions, supervisor or third party reports, licenses, previous training records, observation and questioning. Evidence must be authentic and current, and overseas evidence may need mapping to local legislative requirements such as work health and safety laws.

faqs.q: Can a workplace use RPL for internal training?
faqs.a: Yes, in principle. An employer can recognize existing competence against its own competency framework and skip training that is not needed. The result is not a formal qualification unless a body authorized to award one assesses it against the official standard, but the same evidence principles make the decision defensible.

faqs.q: Does RPL apply in higher education?
faqs.a: Yes. The AQF definition applies across all sectors, and the European [Standards and Guidelines for Quality Assurance](https://www.enqa.eu/wp-content/uploads/2015/11/ESG_2015.pdf) describe fair recognition of prior learning, "including the recognition of non-formal and informal learning", as essential to student progression. Universities and other higher education providers grant credit or advanced standing on the basis of prior learning. Each provider sets its own policy and must maintain the integrity of qualification outcomes.
